title: Remulla dismisses rumors Romualdez set to post bail
summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday quashed rumors that former House speaker Martin Romualdez would be able to post bail soon in relation to the detained leader's P7.4-billion plunder case.

blocks.text: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday quashed rumors that former House speaker Martin Romualdez would be able to post bail soon in relation to the detained leader's P7.4-billion plunder case.
Speaking on his radio program, Remulla said he was aware of such rumors circulating in legal and judicial circles.

"Ngayon, mayroong may matinding kumakalat, ito dididretsuhin ko na: baka raw makakuha ng piyansa 'yung isang suspek natin na nakakakulong ngayon, na malaki, the biggest, in other words that's Martin Romualdez. Pinapakalat nila 'yan. Propaganda. Parang gusto nilang kondisyunin na 'wag kayo magugulat kung makakuha ng [piyansa]. Pero kami we're vigorously opposing that," Remulla said.

(Now, there is something intense going around, I'll get straight to the point. There's talk that one of our incarcerated suspects, a big one, the biggest, in other words, that's Martin Romualdez, has a chance of posting bail. They are spreading that. Propaganda. They want to condition us to not be surprised if he is granted [bail]. But we're vigorously opposing that.)
Remulla said they will not be swayed by propaganda, saying it has been attempted before but the Ombudsman's strategy will not be ruined.

The Ombudsman said the Sandiganbayan has already allowed Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. President Felicito Guevarra to be removed as a co-accused in Romualdez's case. The Sandiganbayan Third Division has approved the amended charge sheet dropping Guevarra, who surrendered to authorities earlier in November.

Guevarra was previously declared as an Ombudsman witness after he returned the money he allegedly processed for Romualdez. He supposedly got some P373 million, which is 1% for every transaction he processed.
This meant that he handled around P37 billion, according to Remulla.
Remulla alluded to people attempting to locate the witness, saying there was also a case where they attempted to impersonate Sandiganbayan Judge Karl Miranda, who was handling Romualdez's case.
"May nag-impersonation ng isang justice… Somebody was trying to impersonate Justice Karl Miranda and trying to get the whereabouts of our witness," Remulla said.
(Someone was impersonating a justice… Somebody was trying to impersonate Justice Karl Miranda and trying to get the whereabouts of our witness.)
Remulla even posited that former National Bureau of Investigation officials were being used to locate the witness.
GMA News has reached out to Romualdez's office and will update the story once they respond. — VDV, GMA News
